alignments.shared_gap: AI-generated work product (specs, architecture docs) lacks built-in human verification affordances — the team has no standard mechanism for confirming that Claude-authored content is correct before it becomes ground truth for decisions.

End-to-end observability for the meta-system is broken in both directions: Kshitiz (the system operator) lacks a verifiable readiness signal before deployment, and Pranav (a team member) cannot see what the system captures about his own work. Neither side of the loop has self-service visibility.

The team lacks a standard mechanism for detecting when Claude introduces errors into logically correct structures — Pranav experienced this in the rule builder (incorrect AND/OR advice), and Ankit-S is proactively building a spec-level control to prevent it from happening in specs.

Both are trying to determine whether a running system's current behavior matches its intended design — Kshitiz for Mycelium v1 vs the living systems architecture, Pranav for the copilot rule-creation infrastructure. Neither has authoritative process documentation to do this without reading logs and source code.

Abhishek is actively evaluating Nango as an architectural decision, but it has not been captured in any knowledge base entry — creating an invisible blind spot that Kshitiz's cycle completeness audit should surface but currently misses.
